intro: This is where half-formed ideas live. Experiments, research notes, and questions I haven't answered yet.

items.title: MechLang
items.description: A domain-specific language for representing and rendering organic reaction mechanisms. Currently refining the parser, molecular representation, rendering system, and mechanism syntax.

items.title: Attention Drift Detection
items.description: Exploring whether observable reading behavior such as scrolling, pauses, backtracking, and tab switching can provide a useful estimate of attention drift without collecting sensitive data.

items.title: Scattering-Theory Reconstruction
items.description: Reconstructing the mathematical path from long-range polarization potentials to low-energy scattering behavior while comparing the derivation with established literature.

items.title: Argon–Krypton Electron Gain Enthalpy
items.description: Tracing the origin and physical meaning of the apparently identical textbook values for argon and krypton, including historical electron-affinity measurements and scattering-theory interpretations.

items.title: AI and Scientific Discovery
items.description: Exploring whether computational systems can help discover useful mathematical structure or physical hypotheses rather than simply predict known outcomes.

items.title: Can a machine discover physics?
items.description: If a system is given observations and enough structural constraints, how much of a physical theory could it rediscover without being explicitly given the governing equations?

items.title: What makes a question worth researching?
items.description: How do you distinguish a question that merely sounds interesting from one that can actually produce new understanding?

items.title: Quantum scattering and low-energy physics
items.description: Primary literature and theoretical treatments relevant to the argon–krypton investigation.

items.title: Scientific machine learning and symbolic regression
items.description: Papers and resources on using computational methods to discover structure in scientific data.
